title: Laureate Education Stock Up 70% as Fund Trims $9 Million Stake Amid $1.7 Billion Revenue Outlook
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: First Sabrepoint Capital Management reduced its stake in Laureate Education by 300,000 shares (worth $9.26 million) in Q4 2025, though the fund still maintains a 6.4% position. Despite the trim, Laureate Education shares have surged 70.8% over the past year, with the company delivering strong Q3 revenue growth of 9% to $400.2 million and raising full-year guidance to $1.686 billion in revenue. The reduction appears to be portfolio rebalancing rather than a loss of confidence in the business.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mentioned only in disclosure policy as a company The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends; no substantive news or analysis provided about the company.

Stock up 70.8% over the past year, strong Q3 revenue growth of 9%, raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.686 billion, 7% year-to-date enrollment growth with Peru up 13%, positive cash flow generation ($272.8 million in first nine months), and expanded share repurchase authorization. Fund's stake reduction appears to be prudent rebalancing after strong performance rather than a negative signal.

title: Laureate (LAUR) Q2 Revenue Jumps 5%
author: Jesterai
description: Laureate Education reported Q2 2025 revenue of $524.2 million, a 5% year-over-year increase, beating analyst estimates. Despite strong enrollment growth and digital learning advances, GAAP earnings were impacted by foreign currency translation losses.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed financial performance with revenue growth and strong enrollment, but reduced by foreign currency translation losses and lower GAAP earnings. Management raised full-year guidance, indicating confidence in business fundamentals.

title: Laureate Education Announces New $100 Million Share Repurchase Program
author: N/A
description: Laureate Education, Inc. announced a new $100 million stock repurchase program, building on its previous $100 million program. The company plans to finance the repurchases using free cash flow, excess cash, and available credit facility capacity.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company is announcing a new stock repurchase program, which indicates confidence in its financial position and a commitment to returning capital to shareholders. The use of free cash flow, excess cash, and available credit facility capacity to finance the repurchases suggests the company has ample liquidity to support this initiative.
